details: CONFIRMED by reading: bin/ci:62 passes RELAY_INERT_FULL_HOOKS=1 when the outer run is full; bin/ci:36 skips hooks-live only when quick=1 AND RELAY_INERT_FULL_HOOKS is empty,
so the nested run executes it; outcome() (bin/ci:48-49) counts every ^ok line of hook-tests.log, which includes hooks-live's "ok    ..." lines (hooks-live.test.sh:47).
Whether a live model run differs between the two runs is PLAUSIBLE (needs a Haiku miss), but the inert probe exists to prove outcomes do not depend on inert files,
and a live model result is not deterministic. The full relay gate is the release gate, so a spurious red there is reachable on ordinary use. Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: bin/ci:36  if [ "$quick" = 1 ] && [ -z "${RELAY_INERT_FULL_HOOKS:-}" ]; then echo "--- $f (left for the full bin/ci: ...)"; continue; fi
bin/ci:62  ( cd "$work" && env -u RELAY_GATE RELAY_INERT_FULL_HOOKS="$([ "$quick" = 0 ] && echo 1)" bash bin/ci --quick )
plugins/core/tests/hooks-live.test.sh:47  if [ "$2" = 0 ]; then echo "ok    $1"; else echo "FAIL  $1: ..."
lib/relay_gate.py run(): command = binding + args, env RELAY_GATE = head (no args = full bin/ci)
failing_case: `relay gate` with no arguments (full bin/ci, RELAY_GATE set). The outer hook-tests step runs hooks-live (4 claude -p Haiku calls); inert_probe (bin/ci:62)
then runs `bin/ci --quick` with RELAY_INERT_FULL_HOOKS=1, and bin/ci:36 lets hooks-live run again in that nested run. outcome() compares results.txt and
"hook cases ok: N" (hooks-live prints "ok    <name>", counted by ^ok). If Haiku answers one check in one run and misses it in the other, the gate
fails with "FAIL inert: a step's result or the test count changed when only inert files changed", blaming inert files for model variance, and pays
for the live calls twice. Before the change hooks-live never ran in either run (RELAY_CORE_TESTS unset).
Should: the nested inert run never makes a paid live call, and the comparison does not depend on hooks-live's outcome.
fix_hint: Skip hooks-live in every --quick run (drop the RELAY_INERT_FULL_HOOKS exception at bin/ci:36), and have outcome() count ok lines outside the hooks-live section
(e.g. awk from "--- *hooks-live*" to the next "--- " line excluded), so the outer full run and the nested quick run compare the same files. Add a case to
tests/test_ci_hook_tests.py with RELAY_INERT_FULL_HOOKS=1 and --quick asserting no STUB-RAN hooks-live.
pass_cases: 1. Full run under RELAY_GATE: the nested inert run's hook-tests log has no hooks-live run (a stub hooks-live in a test tree, as in tests/test_ci_hook_tests.py, does not print STUB-RAN in the nested log), and the inert step's ok counts compare equal (outcome excludes hooks-live's lines, or the outer count subtracts them).
2. Full run without RELAY_GATE: hooks-live still runs once with HOOKS_LIVE=1 (stub prints STUB-RAN hooks-live).
3. Quick run: hooks-live is not run and the log says "left for the full bin/ci" (tests/test_ci_hook_tests.py case 2 keeps passing).
4. Quick relay gate: inert probe still reports "the same results" (green as in the fb28c3f gate log).
reason: tests/test_ci_hook_tests.py:56 (nested quick run never runs hooks-live) and :61 (full run runs it once, comparison ignores its ok lines); bin/ci skips hooks-live in every quick run; quick cases at :40 keep passing.
findings.summary: a full relay gate now runs the live hooks-live test twice (outer run and the inert probe's nested run) and the inert probe compares their model-dependent ok counts
